findings.claim: adaptOpencode treats every unrecognized name containing an underscore as an MCP tool. OpenCode built-ins or custom tools with underscores (other than experimental_image_generate) get rewritten to mcp__<first>__<rest>, so a policy keyed on an mcp__ prefix could match a non-MCP tool, or a server with an underscore in its name maps to the wrong server (e.g. long_term_query becomes mcp__long__term_query). The exclusion list is a single hard-coded name, so any future built-in with an underscore is silently misclassified.

Tests do not cover a server name containing an underscore, the documented limitation (e.g. long_term_query), nor a tool name with further underscores beyond memorycard_mem_search. The limitation is only stated in a comment, so a change to the cut rule would not be caught.

evidence: Read adaptOpencode in the diff: shell and patch map exactly, experimental_image_generate and mcp__-prefixed names pass, others cut at the first underscore.
Usage, README, CHANGELOG and error messages consistently add opencode; tests updated to the new message text.
claude and codex branches are unchanged, and the new test asserts opencode names stay opaque to them.
